items.abstract: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Disease Surveillance and Outbreak Prediction: A Scoping Review Reporting Standards: JBI Scoping Review Methodology and PRISMA-ScR Guidelines 1. Purpose & Rationale Timely detection and accurate prediction of infectious disease threats are paramount for global health security and emergency response. While the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the deployment of artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning, and transformer architectures in public health, a substantial gap remains between high-performing algorithmic models and their operational integration into frontline surveillance systems. The primary purpose of this research is to systematically map, synthesize, and evaluate the current body of literature on AI-enabled infectious disease surveillance. The project establishes a structured functional taxonomy of computational architectures, evaluates their early-warning capability and predictive lead times, and systematically maps the implementation, governance, and structural barriers that prevent these tools from being seamlessly translated into public health policy and routine health system operations. 2. Research Objectives & Specific Questions The project addresses the following primary research question: *What evidence exists regarding the application of artificial intelligence and computational models for infectious disease surveillance, early detection, outbreak prediction, and surveillance optimization, and what implementation challenges influence their operational integration into public health systems? Specific Research Sub-objectives: 1. Algorithmic Classification: Categorize current AI, machine learning, and deep learning architectures (e.g., CNNs, LSTMs, Transformers, Graph Active Learning) deployed across diverse viral and bacterial pathogen threats. 2. Predictive Performance & Lead-Time Analysis:Evaluate empirical metrics (such as AUROC, sensitivity, and lead time in days or weeks) demonstrated by models in early-warning variant detection and outbreak forecasting. 3. Resource Allocation & Health Systems Optimization:** Assess how computational models optimize pass-through surveillance functions, such as diagnostic site selection, laboratory testing workflows, and supply allocation in resource-constrained health settings. 4. Implementation & Governance Bottlenecks:** Identify key structural, data-latency, ethical, and workforce barriers restricting model integration into routine national public health decision-making. 3. Methodological Overview PCC Eligibility Framework: Population: Human populations or simulated population networks impacted by communicable disease threats. Concept: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, sequence transformers, or computational frameworks applied to surveillance, early warning, outbreak forecasting, or surveillance resource allocation. Context:Global public health surveillance systems, encompassing digital infrastructures in high-income settings and health facility frameworks in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Information Sources & Search Strategy: Multi-database searches across PubMed, MEDLINE, and Google Scholar, complemented by grey literature searches of international public health repositories (WHO, CDC, ECDC) and preprint servers (bioRxiv, medRxiv). Screening Governance: Independent title, abstract, and full-text screening conducted by two independent reviewers, with third-reviewer arbitration for consensus. Quality & Risk of Bias Assessment: Methodological quality evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklists and the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST). 4. Expected Outcomes & Public Health Impact** 1. Standardized Functional Taxonomy: A multi-domain framework categorizing AI applications across core surveillance functions ranging from early warning genomic variant prioritization topassive digital anomaly detection. 2.Empirical Performance Evidence Base: A synthesized matrix detailing lead-time advantages and accuracy trade-offs across various algorithmic classes and epidemiological data modalities (e.g., genomic sequences, clinical imaging, mobility streams). 3. Implementation & Policy Roadmap: A comprehensive evaluation of operational bottlenecks, providing health ministries and global health organizations with actionable recommendations to bridge the gap between "black-box" model development and field deployment.

items.title: Leveraging Large Language Model for Ambiguity Detection and Resolution in Software Requirement Specifications
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Ambiguities in software requirement documents, such as software requirement specifications (SRS) and user stories, pose significant challenges to the success of software development projects. These ambiguities often result in misinterpretations, inconsistent system designs, and increased costs and delays. Despite advancements in requirements engineering and natural language processing, existing methods frequently address only limited types of ambiguities or fail to integrate detection and resolution processes effectively. Aims This research introduces a framework that leverages fine‐tuned large language models (LLMs) to systematically detect and resolve ambiguities in software requirements. The framework targets seven key categories of ambiguities: semantic, syntactic, functional, operational, scope, temporal, and quality. Materials and Methods The framework uses fine‐tuned LLaMA 3 and LLaMA 3.1 models with parameter‐efficient LoRA adapters. A diverse dataset of annotated SRS documents and user stories was developed to evaluate the framework. Ambiguity classification was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores, while ambiguity resolution was assessed using BLEU, ROUGE, and BERTScore metrics, complemented by manual evaluation. Results The fine‐tuned models demonstrated substantial improvements in ambiguity classification and generated clear, unambiguous alternatives for ambiguous requirements. The evaluation results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying and resolving ambiguities across the targeted categories. Discussion The findings demonstrate that fine‐tuned LLMs can support comprehensive ambiguity detection and resolution across multiple software requirement formats. The framework improves the clarity and usability of requirements and can support more effective communication among software development stakeholders. Conclusion The proposed framework provides a practical solution for improving the quality of requirements documentation and addressing ambiguities across diverse formats. It can help minimize errors and enhance stakeholder communication in both agile and traditional development environments. Future research will focus on extending the framework's scalability and adaptability to diverse contexts and domain‐specific requirements.

items.title: Life Preservation and Political Resolve: New Human Rights as a Framework for Effective and Bounded Political Action
items.abstract: This conceptual article develops the political implications of Jean-Pol Martin’s New Human Rights (NMR). Its central question is: if preserving human life, meeting fundamental needs and maintaining shared life-supporting conditions are accepted as binding political aims, what responsibilities follow when these conditions are systematically threatened? The framework draws on six equally important fundamental needs: thinking, health, security, social inclusion, self-realisation and participation, and meaning. It distinguishes an anthropological account of human life, an explicit normative commitment to protecting that life, and the assessment of particular political measures. The article’s specific contribution is to use the NMR both as reasons for decisive protection and as constraints on the power exercised in its name. It proposes a six-step assessment procedure addressing evidence of threats, responsibility, feasible alternatives, authority and proportionality, effects on all six needs, and implementation with ongoing review. The consequences of inaction are included alongside those of intervention. Prevention, reliability and sustainability provide the temporal orientation. Within the growing Zenodo corpus on Jean-Pol Martin’s semantic field, the article connects the anthropological and normative foundations of NMR/LdL with political protection and enforcement responsibility. It extends the preceding argument for worldwide orientation by examining how that orientation can guide effective, accountable and revisable action. Hypothetical examples illustrate civic protection, targeted restrictions on violent networks and the preservation of ecological conditions. The article presents a normative reconstruction and a proposed assessment framework; it does not claim empirical validation or establish liability in particular cases. Jean-Pol Martin supplied the theoretical framework and direction of the argument. ChatGPT assisted with conceptual reconstruction, drafting and document production. items.title: Lifecycle costs of safety instrumented systems in process industries: a systematic literature review
items.abstract: A safety instrumented system (SIS) is an automated system designed to detect and mitigate potential risk of hazardous conditions in industrial processes by taking actions to prevent or mitigate incidents. It is essential because it helps protect people, equipment, and the environment by reducing the risk of accidents in hazardous operations, such as in chemical plants, oil refineries, or power stations. While the primary objective of SIS design is safety, economic considerations, particularly lifecycle cost, play a pivotal role in decision-making during the design phase. Although research efforts exist to incorporate lifecycle cost with safety, the literature is fragmented and lacks a comprehensive lifecycle cost framework. Therefore, a systematic literature review is conducted to uncover safety instrumented systems’ lifecycle cost elements and the decision variables that impact them. The review results lead to a comprehensive and structured cost calculation framework to assess SIS designed to protect a process unit economically. Finally, this study provides perspectives on potential research directions relevant to SIS lifecycle cost, including the impact of systematic failures, cybersecurity integration, the relative weighting of different cost elements, inclusion of risk costs, and various SIS application types.

items.title: LineupRL: Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Time Series Captioning via Caption-to-Series Identification
items.abstract: Time series captioning is a fundamental step in time series understanding and can also serve as the bridge between signal and natural language. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) relies on a larger model's captions and cannot exceed their quality. Reinforcement learning (RL) can, but its rewards were designed for other modalities and other tasks, and they transfer poorly to open-ended generation in the time series domain. We address this by proposing LineupRL, a reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) pipeline whose reward is caption-to-series identification. The reward model is a frozen large language model (LLM) verifier that reads the generated caption and the candidate time series as raw values, never the chart, and must pick the described time series from multiple distractors. Matching is a far lighter demand on the verifier than writing questions or judging a caption, so an off-the-shelf LLM can supply the reward. Across two captioning benchmarks, and on forecasting and reconstruction where the predictor sees only the caption, LineupRL outperforms SFT and RL baselines on every metric. The 3B vision language model (VLM) trained by LineupRL also outperforms, at 1/24 of the parameters, the 72B VLM whose captions the SFT baseline is distilled from. Our case study shows that LineupRL resists reward hacking, and that the captioner it trains both traces the trend and names the values at key points.

items.title: Linking Emotional Intelligence and Achievement Motivation in School Students: A Review of Correlates and Implications for Social and Emotional Learning
items.abstract: Achievement motivation and emotional intelligence (EI) are increasingly regarded as central to student success beyond cognitive ability. This review synthesises theoretical and empirical literature on the correlates of achievement motivation and EI among school students, with attention to their interrelationship, demographic and contextual correlates, and implications for practice in the Indian school system. Drawing on classical motivation theories, ability and trait models of EI, meta-analyses and selected school-based studies, the review finds that EI shows a small-to-moderate positive association with academic performance and a consistent positive association with adaptive motivational orientations such as self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation and persistence. Gender, age, parental involvement, school climate and socioeconomic background emerge as important correlates, although findings are often inconsistent. Methodological limitations, including overreliance on self-report, cross-sectional designs and heterogeneous measurement, restrict causal inference. The review concludes that integrating social and emotional learning into curricula and teacher preparation is a promising, evidence-informed strategy, and it identifies priorities for future longitudinal and culturally grounded research.

items.title: LiteEMG-FM: An Efficient and Deployable Foundation Model for Robust EMG Sensing
items.abstract: Electromyography (EMG) signals vary substantially across individuals, body regions, recording sessions, and sensing hardware, limiting the generalization of models for assistive devices and human-computer interaction. Existing time-series foundation models are also computationally expensive for real-time wearable deployment and often fail to capture EMG-specific time-frequency characteristics. We present LiteEMG-FM, an efficient hybrid CNN-Transformer foundation model for practical EMG sensing. Pretrained on 16 diverse upper- and lower-limb EMG datasets, LiteEMG-FM learns representations that generalize across users and datasets. For resource-constrained deployment, we implement a hierarchical wake-up architecture in which a lightweight, always-on 1D-CNN filters rest and non-target activity and activates LiteEMG-FM only for valid gestures. We evaluate full inference offloading, split inference, and full on-device processing, characterizing their trade-offs in latency, power consumption, and memory footprint. Across diverse evaluation settings, LiteEMG-FM outperforms state-of-the-art time-series foundation models and supervised baselines, particularly under zero-calibration cross-participant and data-scarce conditions. These results demonstrate that LiteEMG-FM is an effective, efficient, and deployable foundation model for EMG applications.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Discovery of Typed Semantic Links for Ontology Network Construction
items.abstract: Constructing typed, justified semantic links between ontologies is essential for enabling interoperability across heterogeneous and interdisciplinary knowledge domains. However, manually curating such links is difficult to scale. To address this challenge, we propose an end-to-end framework for ontology network construction that automates the discovery and generation of both intra-domain and inter-domain relationships. Our approach combines domain-adapted DistilBERT embeddings for dense contextual representation, clustering-based pre-filtering to reduce the candidate search space, and GPT-4o-driven relationship generation via iterative prompt engineering to produce semantically rich, interpretable links. Applied to ReproduceMeON - a network of 33 ontologies spanning machine learning, microscopy, computational science, and experimental workflow - the pipeline reduces approximately 800k raw concept pairs to 95k high-quality candidates. Human expert validation of 429 generated relationships by two independent annotators yields an overall precision of 80.19% (91.49% on high-certainty annotations) and an F1 of 0.890, with substantial inter-annotator agreement. Comparative experiments against five similarity-based baselines, including Sentence-BERT, show a substantial performance gap (best baseline F1 = 0.581), while an ablation study demonstrates that similarity-based methods alone fail to discriminate valid from invalid relationships (AUC approx 0.5) on the filtered candidate set. These findings highlight the necessity of LLM-based reasoning over concept roles and domain semantics for accurate relationship construction.

items.title: LLM-driven design of physics-constrained constitutive models: Two agents are better than one
items.abstract: Developing constitutive models that capture how materials deform under load traditionally requires years of specialized expertise in continuum mechanics, machine learning, and scientific programming. Large language models (LLMs) have recently been shown to lower this barrier by generating constitutive models on demand, but existing single-agent pipelines lack systematic checks that the resulting models respect fundamental physical laws. To close this gap, we introduce the first multi-agent LLM-driven approach for constitutive model generation: a Creator agent proposes a model tailored to the data, while an Inspector agent critically audits each proposal against nine physical constraints and returns it for refinement whenever a violation is detected. We demonstrate this concept with constitutive artificial neural networks (CANNs) and benchmark it on brain tissue and rubber as isotropic materials, and on porcine skin tissue as a transversely isotropic material with a preferred fiber direction, using two different LLM backbones (Claude Opus 4.7 and Kimi K2.5). Whether a generated model satisfies the physical constraints is assessed numerically, by probing each constraint across a broad sample of deformation states, rotations, and perturbation directions. Adding the Inspector raises the share of exported models that pass all these checks from 90% to 95% for Opus and from 47% to 60% for Kimi. In addition, the generated models are on par with or even surpass expert-designed models in accuracy, extrapolate reliably beyond the training data, and generalize remarkably well to unseen loading paths. Separating generation from inspection thus turns LLM-driven constitutive modeling into a substantially more trustworthy process. The paradigm is deliberately technique-agnostic and scales automatically with advances in LLM capability, opening a promising path toward automated, physics-aware model discovery.

items.title: Local Support Learning
items.abstract: We explore catastrophic forgetting in the context of large pre-trained models. By considering forgetting as a geometric problem in the input space of each weight matrix, we uncover a natural retention objective under which updates produced by gradient-based optimizers are suboptimal. Following this observation, we propose Local Support Learning (LSL), a general-purpose framework that augments gradient-based training for retention of prior capabilities without access to prior data. During a new learning phase, LSL pairs two components with distinct roles: a standard weight adapter, trained as usual to minimize the loss, and a gating function that enables the adapter only on input activations from its own training distribution, making the update local to that distribution. The key challenge is that this gate must route data from all learning phases while training only on data from the current one. We address this with a gate based on a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), whose likelihood decays rapidly away from its training data, giving it a natural tendency to stay closed on data from prior phases. We show that this post-training approach can resolve forgetting in LLMs of up to 7 billion parameters, retaining both pretrained and finetuned capabilities across multiple training phases, while being efficient in memory and compute, robust to hyperparameter choice, and showing scaling potential.

items.title: Localization of acoustic emission sources in a four-point bending test on a reinforced concrete beam using artificial intelligence
items.abstract: In the field of Acoustic Emission analysis, the use of artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly important. Especially for localizing Acoustic Emission events via pattern recognition of time signals, Neural Networks hold great potential. As part of this research, this potential was tested by examining the locatability of Acoustic Emission sources on a reinforced concrete beam as a result of a four-point bending test. Specifically, the experiment involved a loading that increased until fracture of the specimen, while Acoustic Emissions were measured and recorded over 16 Acoustic Emission sensors. A total of 10,343 Acoustic Emission events were captured, of which 4,102 events could be localized three-dimensionally by triangulation. The remaining 6,241 events could not be assigned locations due to either insufficient determinability of the arrival times or too large measurement deviations. In this work, the combination of neural methods from supervised and unsupervised learning was explored. The acquired events were first divided into localized and non-localized signals. The localized events were subsequently grouped into 5, 10, 15, and 20 clusters using the K-means algorithm (unsupervised learning). Furthermore, four convolutional neural networks were trained by using the clusters as classes and the assigned events as samples per class. This approach achieved assignability with an accuracy of 71–94% and allowed the previously non-localizable Acoustic Emission events to be classified and localized by these Convolutional Neural Networks.

items.title: Loop-wise Structural Footwear Design and Optimization Using FEA-informed Deep Learning and Additive Manufacturing for Adaptive Pressure Distribution with Improved Comfort
items.abstract: This study presents a loop-wise FEA-DL teaming approach for the design and optimization of additive manufacturing-fabricated metamaterial (MM) shoe soles. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and deep learning (DL), this study aims to generate lattice geometries that approximate a prescribed target deformation field to achieve personalized comfort and biomechanical performance. Plantar pressure data is used to generate and optimize metamaterial geometries toward target deformation fields associated with improved ergonomic and medical outcomes. The DL model is enhanced to efficiently handle large-scale three-dimensional data, and a loop-wise refinement strategy is implemented to perform iterative correction of predicted geometries through FEA feedback. By formulating the deformation targets based on biomechanical comfort criteria, the proposed framework can generate geometries ensuring both mechanical functionality and adaptability to individual wearers. A loop optimization strategy is further introduced, allowing the framework to continuously improve the accuracy of geometry prediction from deformation response through repeated learning cycles. Experimental and simulation results demonstrate that the first optimization loop significantly reduced deformation-target mismatch relative to the linearly interpolated baseline designs. However, additional iterations do not consistently yield monotonic improvement. The resulting geometries are compatible with additive manufacturing processes, enabling direct fabrication of customized footwear. This framework establishes a generalizable pathway for applying AM and DL to bio-inspired, user-specific medical or customizable wearables.
